items.title: Cisco gives engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite legacy code
items.summary: Cisco's president announced a groundbreaking initiative allowing a young engineer to utilize unlimited AI tokens for rewriting legacy code. This move highlights the increasing reliance on AI tools in modern software development and the potential for significant efficiency gains.

items.title: Cloudflare Turnstile solver library (no headless browser required)
items.summary: A new open-source library has been released that allows developers to solve Cloudflare's Turnstile CAPTCHA without the need for a headless browser. This simplifies the process of bypassing CAPTCHA challenges, enhancing user experience and automation capabilities.

items.title: Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
items.summary: A developer has shared a project on Hacker News that implements a working Nintendo emulator using approximately 1GB of Qwen weights. This showcases the potential of lightweight models in gaming and opens new avenues for retro gaming enthusiasts.

items.title: Florilegium: Procedural Flowers in LaTeX
items.summary: The Florilegium project introduces a new way to create procedural flowers using LaTeX, enhancing the capabilities of document preparation systems. This tool can be particularly useful for researchers and educators looking to include complex graphics in their work.

items.title: Molly(Signal fork) has not been updated since 3 months and is vulnerable
items.summary: The Signal fork, Molly, has been flagged for not receiving updates for over three months, exposing users to potential security vulnerabilities. Developers and users should be aware of this risk and consider alternatives or updates to ensure data protection.
